title: Editor panels
description: Where Edit’s panels could go next.

paragraphs:
Editor panels
11 November 2026
Edit has seventeen registered panels. They are well made, and they are also the thing the product vision wants less of. These four proposals keep what the panels know and change where it appears.

sections.title: Bring the panel to the block

paragraphs: Today, changing an image’s aspect ratio means opening the Image panel, which floats wherever you last left it. The control and the thing it changes are in different places, and the panel covers part of the page you are judging.

The format bar and the gap pill already solve this for text and spacing: a small bar that belongs to the selection. I would give media the same thing. Selecting a block raises a bar above it with the two or three settings used most. Everything else stays one menu away, and the full panel remains for the long tail.
This is the smallest step toward hands-on Edit, because it reuses the bar surface, the segmented control and the menu exactly as they are.
Click the image. Change the ratio, toggle Crop, open the menu. Esc steps back out.

sections.title: Show where a value comes from

paragraphs: Every media panel has a Desktop, Tablet and Mobile switch. Values fall through from the wider viewport unless a narrower one sets its own. That model is right, but it is invisible: you cannot tell which viewports have overrides, whether the value in front of you is set here or inherited, or how to get back.

Three small marks fix it. A dot on a viewport that has its own values. Inherited values drawn in the optional-metadata ink with the source named beside the label. A reset glyph that appears only on an overridden field, and on a slider a tick where the inherited value sits so you can see how far you have moved.
#127 asks for this on the video editor. I would settle it once as a pattern so every panel reads the same way.
Switch to Tablet: both values are inherited from Desktop. Change one, then reset it. Mobile starts with its own ratio.

sections.title: Turn the save bar into a ledger

paragraphs: The save bar says “3 unsaved changes” and offers to revert all of them. The editor already knows what each change is: Save sends a semantic manifest, and the publisher uses it to write the commit subject. The author is the one person who never sees that list.

Make the count a control. It opens the list, each row names the block and what happened to it, and each row can be reverted alone. This matters more as Edit goes online and as other people use it: “revert everything” is a blunt instrument when one of four changes was a mistake.
It also gives undo of structural edits somewhere to live while #80 and #132 are open.
Open the count. Revert one row, then Save. Reset restores the four changes.
Online Edit at full parity means editing from a phone. A floating panel cannot work there: it is wider than the screen is comfortable with and it is moved by dragging a title bar.

The panel body does not need to change. Put the same fields in a sheet that rises from the bottom edge and stops at three heights. The important behaviour is the one that keeps Edit WYSIWYG: the page scrolls so the block being edited stays visible above the sheet at every height. You are still looking at the real page while you change it.

Controls inside the sheet take the 44px touch minimum; nothing else about them is different. If panels are written as a body plus a container, the desktop panel and the phone sheet are the same component.
Drag the grip, or tap it to step through the three heights. Change the ratio and watch the page keep the image in view.
Esc as one ladder. #84 wants Esc to mean “up one level”. With on-canvas bars the ladder is short and legible: menu, crop, selection, Edit.
Right-click to edit. #92 fits the same bar. The context menu is the bar’s overflow menu, opened at the pointer.
Animate panel size. #93. The deep-dive block in the next report uses grid rows to animate height without measuring; panels can use the same technique.
Rename Dev to Edit. #83. Worth doing before the body and container split, so the new pieces are named for the product.

Inherited values, because it is a pattern and not a feature, it touches every panel a little, and the slider it needs is already wanted. Then the image bar. The ledger is the most valuable for other people, and the sheet is the one to design now and build when online Edit is scheduled.
